"""CodeGraphContext provider setup facade."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from agents_remember.kernel.primitives.identity import (
    provider_instance_id,
    provider_ownership_labels,
    scoped_name,
)
from agents_remember.providers.cgc.seed import (
    CGC_PROVIDER_ID,
    cgc_extra_args,
    cgc_seed_bundle,
)
from agents_remember.providers.context import (
    CGC_NETWORK_NAME,
    CGC_WATCHER_CONTAINER_PREFIX,
)
from agents_remember.providers.setup_common import (
    LifecycleCommand,
    provider_settings,
    run_lifecycle,
    selected_provider_enabled,
    setup_progress_from,
    stable_provider_id,
)
from agents_remember.providers.setup_progress import SetupProgress


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class IsolatedCgcOptions:
    runtime_root: Path | None = None
    settings_path: Path | None = None
    container_name: str | None = None


def isolated_cgc_settings(
    args: Any,
    settings: dict[str, Any],
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    if args.cgc_isolated_runtime_root is None:
        return None

    provider = provider_settings(settings, CGC_PROVIDER_ID)
    if provider is None:
        return None
    _require_isolated_target_root(args)
    cgc = _isolated_cgc_provider(args, provider)
    return _isolated_settings_payload(cgc)


def _require_isolated_target_root(args: Any) -> None:
    if args.cgc_seed_target_repo_root is None:
        raise RuntimeError("--cgc-isolated-runtime-root requires --cgc-seed-target-repo-root")


def _isolated_settings_payload(cgc: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "version": 1,
        "contextProviders": {
            "enabled": True,
            "providers": {
                CGC_PROVIDER_ID: cgc,
            },
            "policy": {
                "discoveryOnly": True,
                "sourceProofRequired": True,
            },
        },
    }


def _isolated_cgc_provider(args: Any, provider: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    isolated_root = args.cgc_isolated_runtime_root.resolve()
    repo_id = stable_provider_id(args.cgc_seed_repo_id or args.cgc_seed_target_repo_root.name)
    instance_id = provider_instance_id(
        "worktree",
        isolated_root,
        workspace_name=args.coordination_root.parent.name,
    )
    cgc = json.loads(json.dumps(provider))
    cgc.update(_isolated_cgc_base_fields(args, isolated_root, repo_id, instance_id))
    cgc["runtime"] = _isolated_cgc_runtime(cgc.get("runtime"), instance_id)
    cgc["backend"] = _isolated_cgc_backend(
        args,
        cgc.get("backend"),
        isolated_root,
        repo_id,
        instance_id,
    )
    return cgc


def _isolated_cgc_base_fields(
    args: Any,
    isolated_root: Path,
    repo_id: str,
    instance_id: str,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    runtime_root = isolated_root / "providers" / "runners" / "codegraphcontext" / instance_id
    log_file = (
        isolated_root
        / "logs"
        / "providers"
        / "codegraphcontext"
        / instance_id
        / "<repoId>"
        / "watch.log"
    )
    return {
        "enabled": True,
        "instance": {
            "id": instance_id,
            "scope": "worktree",
            "labels": provider_ownership_labels(
                provider_id=CGC_PROVIDER_ID,
                instance_id=instance_id,
                scope="worktree",
                coordination_root=args.coordination_root,
            ),
        },
        "roots": [
            {
                "repoId": repo_id,
                "path": args.cgc_seed_target_repo_root.resolve().as_posix(),
            }
        ],
        "runtimeRoot": runtime_root.as_posix(),
        "instanceRootTemplate": "<runtimeRoot>/<repoId>",
        "requirementsFile": (
            args.coordination_root / "providers" / "requirements" / "codegraphcontext.txt"
        ).as_posix(),
        "patchesRoot": (
            args.coordination_root / "providers" / "patches" / "codegraphcontext"
        ).as_posix(),
        "stateFileTemplate": "<instanceRoot>/provider-state.json",
        "watch": {
            "mode": "managed-foreground",
            "cwdTemplate": "<instanceRoot>",
            "logFileTemplate": log_file.as_posix(),
        },
    }


def _isolated_cgc_runtime(runtime_settings: Any, instance_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    runtime = runtime_settings if isinstance(runtime_settings, dict) else {}
    runtime = dict(runtime)
    runner = runtime.get("runner")
    runner = dict(runner) if isinstance(runner, dict) else {}
    runner["buildRoot"] = "<runtimeRoot>/image"
    runner["containerNameTemplate"] = (
        f"{scoped_name(CGC_WATCHER_CONTAINER_PREFIX, instance_id)}-<repoId>"
    )
    runtime["mode"] = "docker"
    runtime["composeProject"] = scoped_name("agents-remember-cgc", instance_id)
    runtime["runner"] = runner
    return runtime


def _isolated_cgc_backend(
    args: Any,
    backend_settings: Any,
    isolated_root: Path,
    repo_id: str,
    instance_id: str,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    backend = backend_settings if isinstance(backend_settings, dict) else {}
    backend = dict(backend)
    backend.update(
        {
            "runtimeRoot": (
                isolated_root / "providers" / "data" / "codegraphcontext" / instance_id / "falkordb"
            ).as_posix(),
            "dataRoot": "<backendRuntimeRoot>/data",
            "imageLockFile": (
                isolated_root
                / "providers"
                / "requirements"
                / "codegraphcontext-falkordb-docker.lock"
            ).as_posix(),
            "containerName": _isolated_cgc_container_name(args, instance_id, repo_id),
            "network": {"name": scoped_name(CGC_NETWORK_NAME, instance_id)},
        }
    )
    return backend


def _isolated_cgc_container_name(args: Any, instance_id: str, repo_id: str) -> str:
    return args.cgc_isolated_container_name or scoped_name("ar-cgc-falkordb", instance_id, repo_id)


def write_isolated_cgc_settings(
    args: Any,
    settings: dict[str, Any],
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    data = isolated_cgc_settings(args, settings)
    if data is None:
        args.cgc_from_settings = None
        return None

    path = args.cgc_isolated_settings_path or (
        args.cgc_isolated_runtime_root.resolve()
        / "settings"
        / "codegraphcontext-provider-settings.json"
    )
    args.cgc_from_settings = path.resolve()
    if not args.dry_run:
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return {
        "path": args.cgc_from_settings.as_posix(),
        "dryRun": args.dry_run,
        "settings": data if args.dry_run else None,
    }


def install_enabled_provider(args: Any, settings: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    if not selected_provider_enabled(args, settings, CGC_PROVIDER_ID):
        return []
    progress = setup_progress_from(args)
    progress.phase_start("codegraphcontext", "install-all")
    result = run_lifecycle(
        args.coordination_root,
        LifecycleCommand(
            provider="cgc",
            action="install-all",
            extra_args=tuple(cgc_extra_args(args)),
        ),
        timeout=args.timeout,
        dry_run=args.dry_run,
    )
    progress.phase_done(result)
    return [result]


def prepare_enabled_provider(args: Any, settings: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    if not selected_provider_enabled(args, settings, CGC_PROVIDER_ID):
        return []
    progress = setup_progress_from(args)
    progress.phase_start("codegraphcontext", "seed", note="graph copy from workspace (seconds)")
    seed = cgc_seed_bundle(args, settings)
    seed_result = {"provider": "codegraphcontext", "action": "seed", **seed}
    progress.phase_done(seed_result)
    results = [seed_result]
    results.append(_refresh_after_seed(args, seed, progress))
    return results


def _seed_failure_reason(seed: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    reason = seed.get("reason")
    if reason:
        return str(reason)
    stage = seed.get("stage")
    return f"seed failed at {stage}" if stage else "seed failed"


def _refresh_after_seed(args: Any, seed: dict[str, Any], progress: SetupProgress) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if seed.get("ok"):
        return {
            "ok": True,
            "provider": "codegraphcontext",
            "action": "refresh-all",
            "skipped": True,
            "reason": "CGC seed loaded successfully",
        }
    if args.cgc_refresh_fallback:
        # The single most important transition to surface (GitHub #53): a refused
        # seed changes the expected duration from ~1 minute to N minutes, and the
        # reindex itself emits nothing the orchestrator can see.
        progress.phase_start(
            "codegraphcontext",
            "refresh-all",
            note="full reindex fallback; duration scales with repo size (minutes)",
            seed_fallback={"active": True, "reason": _seed_failure_reason(seed)},
        )
        result = run_lifecycle(
            args.coordination_root,
            LifecycleCommand(
                provider="cgc",
                action="refresh-all",
                extra_args=tuple(cgc_extra_args(args)),
            ),
            timeout=args.timeout,
            dry_run=args.dry_run,
        )
        progress.phase_done(result)
        return result
    return {
        "ok": False,
        "provider": "codegraphcontext",
        "action": "refresh-all",
        "skipped": True,
        "reason": "CGC seed failed and refresh fallback is disabled",
    }

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from agents_remember.kernel.primitives.identity import (
    provider_instance_id,
    provider_ownership_labels,
    scoped_name,
)

# Leaf import; see grepai/lifecycle/backend.py for the aggregator-cycle rationale.
from agents_remember.providers.grepai.context import (
    GREPAI_NETWORK_NAME,
    GREPAI_OLLAMA_IMAGE,
    GREPAI_PIN,
    GREPAI_RUNNER_IMAGE_REPOSITORY,
)
from agents_remember.providers.setup_common import provider_settings, stable_provider_id

GREPAI_PROVIDER_ID = "grepai-memory"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class IsolatedGrepaiOptions:
    runtime_root: Path | None = None
    settings_path: Path | None = None
    project_id: str | None = None
    target_memory_root: Path | None = None
    allow_missing_roots: bool = False


def isolated_grepai_settings(args: Any, settings: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    provider = provider_settings(settings, GREPAI_PROVIDER_ID)
    if provider is None or args.grepai_isolated_runtime_root is None:
        return None
    _require_isolated_grepai_target(args)
    isolated_root = args.grepai_isolated_runtime_root.resolve()
    project_id = stable_provider_id(args.grepai_seed_project_id)
    instance_id = provider_instance_id(
        "worktree",
        isolated_root,
        workspace_name=args.coordination_root.parent.name,
    )
    grepai = json.loads(json.dumps(provider))
    grepai.update(
        _isolated_grepai_base_fields(
            args,
            isolated_root=isolated_root,
            instance_id=instance_id,
        )
    )
    grepai["roots"] = _isolated_grepai_roots(
        grepai,
        project_id=project_id,
        target_memory_root=args.grepai_seed_target_memory_root.resolve(),
    )
    grepai["runtime"] = _isolated_grepai_runtime(grepai.get("runtime"), instance_id)
    grepai["backend"] = _isolated_grepai_backend(
        args,
        grepai.get("backend"),
        isolated_root=isolated_root,
        instance_id=instance_id,
    )
    grepai["embedder"] = _isolated_grepai_embedder(
        args,
        grepai.get("embedder"),
        isolated_root=isolated_root,
        instance_id=instance_id,
    )
    return _isolated_settings_payload(grepai)


def _require_isolated_grepai_target(args: Any) -> None:
    if not args.grepai_seed_project_id:
        raise RuntimeError("--grepai-seed-project-id is required for isolated GrepAI")
    if args.grepai_seed_target_memory_root is None:
        raise RuntimeError("--grepai-seed-target-memory-root is required for isolated GrepAI")


def _isolated_settings_payload(grepai: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "version": 1,
        "contextProviders": {
            "enabled": True,
            "providers": {
                GREPAI_PROVIDER_ID: grepai,
            },
            "policy": {
                "discoveryOnly": True,
                "sourceProofRequired": True,
            },
        },
    }


def _isolated_grepai_base_fields(
    args: Any,
    *,
    isolated_root: Path,
    instance_id: str,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    runtime_root = isolated_root / "providers" / "runners" / "grepai" / instance_id
    log_root = isolated_root / "logs" / "providers" / "grepai" / instance_id
    # The grepai logical `workspace` is a key INSIDE the (already isolated) worktree
    # postgres, not a Docker resource name. Scoping it by the worktree instance made the
    # seeded clone (keyed under the workspace `workspace`) invisible to the worktree
    # watcher, forcing a full re-embed. Track the WORKSPACE identity instead so the clone
    # is reused; the worktree instance_id still namespaces every container/network/runtime
    # path below. workspace_name mirrors the proxy the worktree instance_id itself uses.
    workspace_instance_id = provider_instance_id(
        "workspace",
        args.coordination_root,
        workspace_name=args.coordination_root.parent.name,
    )
    return {
        "enabled": True,
        "instance": {
            "id": instance_id,
            "scope": "worktree",
            "labels": provider_ownership_labels(
                provider_id=GREPAI_PROVIDER_ID,
                instance_id=instance_id,
                scope="worktree",
                coordination_root=args.coordination_root,
            ),
        },
        "workspace": scoped_name("agents-remember-memory", workspace_instance_id),
        "runtimeRoot": runtime_root.as_posix(),
        "requirementsFile": (
            args.coordination_root / "providers" / "requirements" / "grepai.txt"
        ).as_posix(),
        "stateFile": (runtime_root / "state" / "provider-state.json").as_posix(),
        "watch": {
            "mode": "background",
            "cwd": (isolated_root / "memory-roots").as_posix(),
            "logDir": log_root.as_posix(),
        },
        "allowMissingRoots": bool(getattr(args, "grepai_allow_missing_roots", False)),
    }


def _isolated_grepai_roots(
    provider: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    project_id: str,
    target_memory_root: Path,
) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    roots = provider.get("roots")
    if not isinstance(roots, list):
        roots = []
    replaced = False
    isolated_roots: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    for root in roots:
        normalized = _normalized_root(root)
        if normalized is None:
            continue
        if normalized["projectId"] == project_id:
            normalized["path"] = target_memory_root.as_posix()
            replaced = True
        isolated_roots.append(normalized)
    if not replaced:
        isolated_roots.append({"projectId": project_id, "path": target_memory_root.as_posix()})
    return isolated_roots


def _normalized_root(root: Any) -> dict[str, str] | None:
    if isinstance(root, str):
        return {"projectId": stable_provider_id(Path(root).name), "path": root}
    if not isinstance(root, dict):
        return None
    raw_path = str(root.get("path", ""))
    if not raw_path:
        return None
    project_id = stable_provider_id(
        str(root.get("projectId") or root.get("repoId") or Path(raw_path).name)
    )
    return {"projectId": project_id, "path": raw_path}


def _isolated_grepai_runtime(runtime_settings: Any, instance_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    version = GREPAI_PIN.split("==", 1)[1]
    runtime = runtime_settings if isinstance(runtime_settings, dict) else {}
    runtime = dict(runtime)
    runner = runtime.get("runner")
    runner = dict(runner) if isinstance(runner, dict) else {}
    runner.update(
        {
            "image": f"{GREPAI_RUNNER_IMAGE_REPOSITORY}:{version}",
            "containerName": scoped_name("ar-grepai-watcher", instance_id),
            "imageLockFile": "<coordination_root>/providers/requirements/grepai-runner-docker.lock",
            "buildRoot": "<runtimeRoot>/image",
            "runtimeMount": "/grepai/runtime",
            "logsMount": "/grepai/logs",
        }
    )
    runtime["mode"] = "docker"
    runtime["composeProject"] = scoped_name("agents-remember-grepai", instance_id)
    runtime["network"] = {"name": scoped_name(GREPAI_NETWORK_NAME, instance_id)}
    runtime["runner"] = runner
    return runtime


def _isolated_grepai_backend(
    args: Any,
    backend_settings: Any,
    *,
    isolated_root: Path,
    instance_id: str,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    backend = backend_settings if isinstance(backend_settings, dict) else {}
    backend = dict(backend)
    backend.update(
        {
            "runtimeRoot": (
                isolated_root / "providers" / "data" / "grepai" / instance_id / "postgres"
            ).as_posix(),
            "dataRoot": "<backendRuntimeRoot>/data",
            "image": "pgvector/pgvector:pg16",
            "imageLockFile": (
                args.coordination_root
                / "providers"
                / "requirements"
                / "grepai-postgres-docker.lock"
            ).as_posix(),
            "containerName": scoped_name("ar-grepai-postgres", instance_id),
            "postgres": {
                "user": "grepai",
                "password": "grepai",
                "database": "grepai",
            },
            "ports": {
                "postgres": {
                    "bindHost": "127.0.0.1",
                    "hostPort": "auto",
                    "containerPort": 5432,
                }
            },
        }
    )
    return backend


def _isolated_grepai_embedder(
    args: Any,
    embedder_settings: Any,
    *,
    isolated_root: Path,
    instance_id: str,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    embedder = embedder_settings if isinstance(embedder_settings, dict) else {}
    embedder = dict(embedder)
    ollama_container = scoped_name("ar-grepai-ollama", instance_id)
    # The worktree ollama starts with an empty model store. Rather than re-pulling the
    # ~274MB embedding model over the network for every worktree, seed it locally from the
    # already-running workspace ollama (the model is immutable shared content; the worktree's
    # vectors stay isolated in its own postgres). The watcher only pulls as a fallback.
    workspace_instance_id = provider_instance_id(
        "workspace",
        args.coordination_root,
        workspace_name=args.coordination_root.parent.name,
    )
    workspace_ollama_container = scoped_name("ar-grepai-ollama", workspace_instance_id)
    backend = embedder.get("backend")
    backend = dict(backend) if isinstance(backend, dict) else {}
    backend.update(
        {
            "mode": "docker",
            "image": GREPAI_OLLAMA_IMAGE,
            "imageLockFile": (
                args.coordination_root / "providers" / "requirements" / "grepai-ollama-docker.lock"
            ).as_posix(),
            "runtimeRoot": (
                isolated_root / "providers" / "data" / "grepai" / instance_id / "ollama"
            ).as_posix(),
            "dataRoot": "<embedderRuntimeRoot>/data",
            "dataDestination": "/root/.ollama",
            "containerName": ollama_container,
            "seedFromContainer": workspace_ollama_container,
            "ports": {
                "http": {
                    "bindHost": "127.0.0.1",
                    "hostPort": "auto",
                    "containerPort": 11434,
                }
            },
        }
    )
    embedder.update(
        {
            "provider": "ollama",
            "model": "nomic-embed-text",
            "endpoint": f"http://{ollama_container}:11434",
            "dimensions": 768,
            "backend": backend,
        }
    )
    return embedder

# Shared STE-inspired writing profile

## Purpose and selected principles

Curators and explainer authors use this single profile for invariant statements, family guarantees,
history reasons and walkthrough prose. It selects clarity principles from
[ASD-STE100](https://asd-ste100.org/about_STE.html); it does not claim full ASD-STE100 compliance,
an "80 percent" measurement or a new controlled-language standard.

Name the actor and use concrete verbs: say who must do what, not merely that something is handled.
Write one independently testable promise per invariant. A paragraph develops one idea. Sentences
normally target about 20–25 words; precision takes priority over sentence length. Keep an exact
technical identifier or essential qualification even when the sentence is longer. Never split an
invariant automatically to meet a word target: a split is an explicit authored semantic change.

State conditions and exceptions explicitly. Keep quantifiers and negation: "every", "only", "no"
and "must not" are part of the obligation, not words to trim. Repeat the same term for the same
concept. Prefer a short explanation to an invented synonym.

## Use the project's vocabulary

Read applicable existing term records and use the product's vocabulary; do not create a second
terminology registry. These explanations orient the author without replacing those records:

| Term | Use |
| --- | --- |
| invariant | One independently testable obligation, with its applicability, conditions and exclusions. |
| family | An authored record whose members support its own joint guarantee; not a directory grouping. |
| joint guarantee | What the members together promise that none promises alone. Do not concatenate their statements. |
| realization | An attributed code place that carries an obligation, with its own rationale and role. |
| proof | Recorded evidence of a particular tested facet; not a claim that every case is established. |
| history row | The existing writer's content-bound judgment about a subject and its change. |
| revision | The exact record version the judgment or comparison addresses; never a prose edit counter supplied by the author. |
| candidate | The exact proposed code and memory state under examination, not an assumed installed or landed state. |

Keep identifiers, quoted source text and admitted effect labels exact. Distinguish
missing, unexamined, unavailable and measured absence: respectively not supplied, not checked,
not readable/obtainable, and checked with no instance found in a stated scope. None establishes
another, and none proves equivalence.

## Separate the promise from its support

State the promise in `statement`. Keep applicability, essential conditions and exclusions in their
existing semantic fields. When the statement relies on those fields, make that connection clear;
read the statement and scope together. Do not remove a condition just because another display shows it.

Keep realizations, proofs, identities and authoring provenance in their existing structural owners.
A history reason explains the concrete change and its consequence; a task ID or "wording improved"
alone explains neither. Use the existing [handoff contract](../templates/curator-handoff-list.md):
producer-owned fields remain verbatim, including the original statement and evidence. Author a
proposed record rewrite separately; do not silently replace the statement the producer handed over.
The writer continues to own IDs, anchors, revisions and row mechanics.

## Independent meaning review before publication

Use the existing [independent fact-check](../criteria/onboarding-memory.md#om-2--independent-fact-check-of-curated-knowledge-second-reader-requirement-bound-mik-r53-rule-5),
not a style-specific gate. A clearer rewrite is never proof of preserved meaning.

1. Preserve the exact old revision, before text, semantic scope, source anchors and evidence identities.
   Bind the proposed text to that baseline and the exact candidate being examined.
2. Compare old and new actor, trigger, required behavior, forbidden behavior, quantifiers, conditions and exclusions.
   Name each facet explicitly, including an unchanged field that the new statement depends on.
3. A reader who wrote none of the drafts explains each promise without oral repair and checks
   concrete conforming, violating and boundary cases against both versions. The reader records
   each ambiguity, changed obligation, missing evidence and unresolved case, not just a verdict.
4. Propose `clarify` only after independent review establishes that the obligation stays the same.
   A real change uses the existing appropriate effect and writer/history/revision route. Do not
   classify an edit from its apparent size or its word count. A family change retains its own
   authored effect, guarantee, examined members and writer-owned revision.
5. Correct or explicitly classify every disputed case before the normal writer publishes.
   An ambiguous draft stays unaccepted and names the actor, quantifier, condition or case in dispute.
   An unreadable revision or missing evidence is a reported gap, never an equivalence judgment.

### Worked comparison and deliberate failures (illustrations, not pilot evidence)

Before: "For every landing, the landing owner must publish only the accepted code and memory trees;
if either tree differs from the accepted candidate, publication must be refused."

Proposed: "For every landing, the landing owner must publish only the accepted code and memory trees.
The owner must refuse publication if either tree differs from the accepted candidate."

The proposed draft names the same actor, every landing, the same allowed trees and the same refusal
trigger. Its author has not accepted equivalence. The independent reader must test at least these cases:

| Case | Required reading of both versions |
| --- | --- |
| Conforming | Both trees equal the accepted candidate: the owner may publish under the existing admission rules. This promise alone does not grant admission. |
| Violating | The owner publishes a different memory tree even though the code tree matches: the owner violates the refusal. |
| Boundary | Only one tree differs: "either" still requires refusal. No exception for a code-only match exists. |

| Draft fault | What the independent comparison must catch |
| --- | --- |
| Removed negation | Changing "must not publish a different tree" to "must publish a different tree" reverses forbidden behavior. |
| Changed quantifier | Replacing "every landing" with "normally at landing" permits previously forbidden exceptions. It is not a clarification. |
| Lost condition | Dropping "if either tree differs" changes the refusal trigger; removing it from scope or omitting its connection in the prose does not preserve it. |
| Unrecorded effect | Calling a changed obligation cosmetic, or publishing it without the appropriate authored effect and history route, leaves the change unaccepted. |
| Altered frozen row | Editing an old closed row to make the draft appear historical changes evidence, not meaning preservation. Retain the original bytes and use the normal new revision route. |

## Three-real-invariant pilot and adoption

Select three existing invariant revisions: a direct promise, a conditional or exception-bearing
promise, and an obligation used in an authored family guarantee. Preserve the exact before text,
revision, scope, source/evidence identities and family membership where relevant. Produce proposed
rewrites and the facet/case comparison above. Record source availability separately from semantic
review: a stored evidence pointer is not evidence that the pointed-to report was read or rerun.

Prototype on real records in shared scratch clones, never the official checkout. Keep a frozen
baseline and separate drafts. An independent reader must judge all three; the author's own table
is a proposal, not acceptance. Correct or classify every ambiguity before the normal admitted
writer publishes. Do not run the writer merely to demonstrate style, rewrite frozen history,
backfill closed rows, or bulk-rewrite existing records. Scratch-clone preparation and later writer
execution require their normal authorization and isolation; this guide grants neither.

After adoption, new or revised invariant statements, family guarantees, history reasons and
walkthrough prose use this profile. Migration authors link it from their procedure before waves
start; preserve every other leaf's required guidance rather than adding a second writing guide.
Existing frozen records and closed history remain inspectable at their original identities.
Guide edits follow normal source/copy checks and curation. The normal skill-copy generator carries
this reference; its composition entry is reference metadata, not another meaning authority.

There is no automatic semantic validator here. Word-count and vocabulary heuristics cannot approve,
reject or classify meaning. Schema, identity, admission, invariant gates and normal writer refusal
and retry behavior remain unchanged. This profile provides author/reviewer guidance and examples,
not a language gate or a closeout bypass.

  'import json; from agents_remember.serving.build_info import process_serving_build; print(json.dumps(process_serving_build().payload().model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True)))'
```

Compare its `version`, `sourceDigest`, `packageRoot`, `pythonExecutable` and `commit` with the
starting stamp before using this CLI to decide or write. A missing identity or a mismatch does
not establish the serving build. Report it; use the mounted tool when it admits the operation.
Keep an unreported commit unknown, never call it a verified clean checkout.

Use the same interpreter and explicit package path for the public CLI commands:

```sh
PYTHONPATH="$AR_SERVING_PARENT" "$AR_SERVING_PYTHON" -P -m agents_remember.cli \
  knowledge-worklist --contract '<this leaf enclosure contract>'
PYTHONPATH="$AR_SERVING_PARENT" "$AR_SERVING_PYTHON" -P -m agents_remember.cli \
  knowledge-ingest --contract '<this leaf enclosure contract>' \
  --list '<the hand-off list>' --authorization-ref '<the admitted authorization>' --commit --json
```

The worklist command computes and persists the leaf's worklist beside its contract. The writer
reads that worklist and the contract's code and memory roots. Without `--commit`, ingest plans,
validates and writes no files; `--commit` authorizes file writes, never a Git commit or acceptance.
The parser has no `--baseline`, `--publish` or `--publish-to` options. Read the actual report state,
written paths, record/entry IDs and refusals: exit zero covers both a plan and a write, and even a
`written` report with no written paths establishes no publication. A correct-input write refusal
uses the procedure linked from the operation's **Failure handling** section.

## Step 2 — check messages

(`realization_rationale_absent`).

The command
   needs converted memory: on the legacy format it refuses with `legacy-format` and names the conversion command.

## Step 2 — weakness and dependent records

**A weakness and a dependent are recorded through the writer, as every record.** An entry of kind `weakness` in a producer's hand-off list becomes a `WKN-` record through the writer, or the report says why not: the writer refuses one without a file, with an unknown kind, or with a statement beyond its one-sentence bound, and the refusal names the field. An entry of kind `dependent` becomes a `DPD-` record: the document, and for each place it stands on the recorded value the writer reads at the task's tip -- a code anchor, a whole file's blob, or an invariant's or a family's revision -- with the confirmation's task, role and commit. Every write of a dependent is a confirmation; no value is typed in. A Curator answers the worklist's row for a weakness (it stands, and the anchor moves with the code; or it is closed) and for a changed document (only the confirmed record answers it). Neither record ever refuses a task.

## Step 3 — family and external-reference format

When you restate a family's
guarantee, name the family in `history` as a `changed` row with your `effect`; the writer fills the
family's own revision.

An external document a card rests on is cited as an
   `external` reference target in the card's sidecar, never as a repository path with a Git blob. Name that
   document in the handoff evidence for the record's `origin`, so the evidence shows which external document
   each backed record rests on.

## Step 3 — read-back call fragment

the records `knowledge_read` with `view="family"` names over this leaf's memory worktree, opened with your own tools

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class IsolatedCgcOptions:
    runtime_root: Path | None = None
    settings_path: Path | None = None
    container_name: str | None = None


def isolated_cgc_settings(
    args: Any,
    settings: dict[str, Any],
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    if args.cgc_isolated_runtime_root is None:
        return None

    provider = provider_settings(settings, CGC_PROVIDER_ID)
    if provider is None:
        return None
    _require_isolated_target_root(args)
    cgc = _isolated_cgc_provider(args, provider)
    return _isolated_settings_payload(cgc)


def _require_isolated_target_root(args: Any) -> None:
    if args.cgc_seed_target_repo_root is None:
        raise RuntimeError("--cgc-isolated-runtime-root requires --cgc-seed-target-repo-root")


def _isolated_settings_payload(cgc: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "version": 1,
        "contextProviders": {
            "enabled": True,
            "providers": {
                CGC_PROVIDER_ID: cgc,
            },
            "policy": {
                "discoveryOnly": True,
                "sourceProofRequired": True,
            },
        },
    }


def _isolated_cgc_provider(args: Any, provider: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    isolated_root = args.cgc_isolated_runtime_root.resolve()
    repo_id = stable_provider_id(args.cgc_seed_repo_id or args.cgc_seed_target_repo_root.name)
    instance_id = provider_instance_id(
        "worktree",
        isolated_root,
        workspace_name=args.coordination_root.parent.name,
    )
    cgc = json.loads(json.dumps(provider))
    cgc.update(_isolated_cgc_base_fields(args, isolated_root, repo_id, instance_id))
    cgc["runtime"] = _isolated_cgc_runtime(cgc.get("runtime"), instance_id)
    cgc["backend"] = _isolated_cgc_backend(
        args,
        cgc.get("backend"),
        isolated_root,
        repo_id,
        instance_id,
    )
    return cgc


def _isolated_cgc_base_fields(
    args: Any,
    isolated_root: Path,
    repo_id: str,
    instance_id: str,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    runtime_root = isolated_root / "providers" / "runners" / "codegraphcontext" / instance_id
    log_file = (
        isolated_root
        / "logs"
        / "providers"
        / "codegraphcontext"
        / instance_id
        / "<repoId>"
        / "watch.log"
    )
    return {
        "enabled": True,
        "instance": {
            "id": instance_id,
            "scope": "worktree",
            "labels": provider_ownership_labels(
                provider_id=CGC_PROVIDER_ID,
                instance_id=instance_id,
                scope="worktree",
                coordination_root=args.coordination_root,
            ),
        },
        "roots": [
            {
                "repoId": repo_id,
                "path": args.cgc_seed_target_repo_root.resolve().as_posix(),
            }
        ],
        "runtimeRoot": runtime_root.as_posix(),
        "instanceRootTemplate": "<runtimeRoot>/<repoId>",
        "requirementsFile": (
            args.coordination_root / "providers" / "requirements" / "codegraphcontext.txt"
        ).as_posix(),
        "patchesRoot": (
            args.coordination_root / "providers" / "patches" / "codegraphcontext"
        ).as_posix(),
        "stateFileTemplate": "<instanceRoot>/provider-state.json",
        "watch": {
            "mode": "managed-foreground",
            "cwdTemplate": "<instanceRoot>",
            "logFileTemplate": log_file.as_posix(),
        },
    }


def _isolated_cgc_runtime(runtime_settings: Any, instance_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    runtime = runtime_settings if isinstance(runtime_settings, dict) else {}
    runtime = dict(runtime)
    runner = runtime.get("runner")
    runner = dict(runner) if isinstance(runner, dict) else {}
    runner["buildRoot"] = "<runtimeRoot>/image"
    runner["containerNameTemplate"] = (
        f"{scoped_name(CGC_WATCHER_CONTAINER_PREFIX, instance_id)}-<repoId>"
    )
    runtime["mode"] = "docker"
    runtime["composeProject"] = scoped_name("agents-remember-cgc", instance_id)
    runtime["runner"] = runner
    return runtime


def _isolated_cgc_backend(
    args: Any,
    backend_settings: Any,
    isolated_root: Path,
    repo_id: str,
    instance_id: str,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    backend = backend_settings if isinstance(backend_settings, dict) else {}
    backend = dict(backend)
    backend.update(
        {
            "runtimeRoot": (
                isolated_root / "providers" / "data" / "codegraphcontext" / instance_id / "falkordb"
            ).as_posix(),
            "dataRoot": "<backendRuntimeRoot>/data",
            "imageLockFile": (
                isolated_root
                / "providers"
                / "requirements"
                / "codegraphcontext-falkordb-docker.lock"
            ).as_posix(),
            "containerName": _isolated_cgc_container_name(args, instance_id, repo_id),
            "network": {"name": scoped_name(CGC_NETWORK_NAME, instance_id)},
        }

    return backend


def _isolated_cgc_container_name(args: Any, instance_id: str, repo_id: str) -> str:
    return args.cgc_isolated_container_name or scoped_name("ar-cgc-falkordb", instance_id, repo_id)


def write_isolated_cgc_settings(
    args: Any,
    settings: dict[str, Any],
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    data = isolated_cgc_settings(args, settings)
    if data is None:
        args.cgc_from_settings = None
        return None

    path = args.cgc_isolated_settings_path or (
        args.cgc_isolated_runtime_root.resolve()
        / "settings"
        / "codegraphcontext-provider-settings.json"
    )
    args.cgc_from_settings = path.resolve()
    if not args.dry_run:
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return {
        "path": args.cgc_from_settings.as_posix(),
        "dryRun": args.dry_run,
        "settings": data if args.dry_run else None,
    }


def install_enabled_provider(args: Any, settings: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    if not selected_provider_enabled(args, settings, CGC_PROVIDER_ID):
        return []
    progress = setup_progress_from(args)
    progress.phase_start("codegraphcontext", "install-all")
    result = run_lifecycle(
        args.coordination_root,
        LifecycleCommand(
            provider="cgc",
            action="install-all",
            extra_args=tuple(cgc_extra_args(args)),
        ),
        timeout=args.timeout,
        dry_run=args.dry_run,
    )
    progress.phase_done(result)
    return [result]


def prepare_enabled_provider(args: Any, settings: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    if not selected_provider_enabled(args, settings, CGC_PROVIDER_ID):
        return []
    progress = setup_progress_from(args)
    progress.phase_start("codegraphcontext", "seed", note="graph copy from workspace (seconds)")
    seed = cgc_seed_bundle(args, settings)
    seed_result = {"provider": "codegraphcontext", "action": "seed", **seed}
    progress.phase_done(seed_result)
    results = [seed_result]
    results.append(_refresh_after_seed(args, seed, progress))
    return results


def _seed_failure_reason(seed: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    reason = seed.get("reason")
    if reason:
        return str(reason)
    stage = seed.get("stage")
    return f"seed failed at {stage}" if stage else "seed failed"


def _refresh_after_seed(args: Any, seed: dict[str, Any], progress: SetupProgress) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if seed.get("ok"):
        return {
            "ok": True,
            "provider": "codegraphcontext",
            "action": "refresh-all",
            "skipped": True,
            "reason": "CGC seed loaded successfully",
        }
    if args.cgc_refresh_fallback:
        # The single most important transition to surface (GitHub #53): a refused
        # seed changes the expected duration from ~1 minute to N minutes, and the
        # reindex itself emits nothing the orchestrator can see.
        progress.phase_start(
            "codegraphcontext",
            "refresh-all",
            note="full reindex fallback; duration scales with repo size (minutes)",
            seed_fallback={"active": True, "reason": _seed_failure_reason(seed)},
        )
        result = run_lifecycle(
            args.coordination_root,
            LifecycleCommand(
                provider="cgc",
                action="refresh-all",
                extra_args=tuple(cgc_extra_args(args)),
            ),
            timeout=args.timeout,
            dry_run=args.dry_run,
        )
        progress.phase_done(result)
        return result
    return {
        "ok": False,
        "provider": "codegraphcontext",
        "action": "refresh-all",
        "skipped": True,
        "reason": "CGC seed failed and refresh fallback is disabled",
    }

GREPAI_PROVIDER_ID = "grepai-memory"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class IsolatedGrepaiOptions:
    runtime_root: Path | None = None
    settings_path: Path | None = None
    project_id: str | None = None
    target_memory_root: Path | None = None
    allow_missing_roots: bool = False


def isolated_grepai_settings(args: Any, settings: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    provider = provider_settings(settings, GREPAI_PROVIDER_ID)
    if provider is None or args.grepai_isolated_runtime_root is None:
        return None
    _require_isolated_grepai_target(args)
    isolated_root = args.grepai_isolated_runtime_root.resolve()
    project_id = stable_provider_id(args.grepai_seed_project_id)
    instance_id = provider_instance_id(
        "worktree",
        isolated_root,
        workspace_name=args.coordination_root.parent.name,
    )
    grepai = json.loads(json.dumps(provider))
    grepai.update(
        _isolated_grepai_base_fields(
            args,
            isolated_root=isolated_root,
            instance_id=instance_id,
        )
    )
    grepai["roots"] = _isolated_grepai_roots(
        grepai,
        project_id=project_id,
        target_memory_root=args.grepai_seed_target_memory_root.resolve(),
    )
    grepai["runtime"] = _isolated_grepai_runtime(grepai.get("runtime"), instance_id)
    grepai["backend"] = _isolated_grepai_backend(
        args,
        grepai.get("backend"),
        isolated_root=isolated_root,
        instance_id=instance_id,
    )
    grepai["embedder"] = _isolated_grepai_embedder(
        args,
        grepai.get("embedder"),
        isolated_root=isolated_root,
        instance_id=instance_id,
    )
    return _isolated_settings_payload(grepai)


def _require_isolated_grepai_target(args: Any) -> None:
    if not args.grepai_seed_project_id:
        raise RuntimeError("--grepai-seed-project-id is required for isolated GrepAI")
    if args.grepai_seed_target_memory_root is None:
        raise RuntimeError("--grepai-seed-target-memory-root is required for isolated GrepAI")


def _isolated_settings_payload(grepai: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "version": 1,
        "contextProviders": {
            "enabled": True,
            "providers": {
                GREPAI_PROVIDER_ID: grepai,
            },
            "policy": {
                "discoveryOnly": True,
                "sourceProofRequired": True,
            },
        },
    }


def _isolated_grepai_base_fields(
    args: Any,
    *,
    isolated_root: Path,
    instance_id: str,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    runtime_root = isolated_root / "providers" / "runners" / "grepai" / instance_id
    log_root = isolated_root / "logs" / "providers" / "grepai" / instance_id
    # The grepai logical `workspace` is a key INSIDE the (already isolated) worktree
    # postgres, not a Docker resource name. Scoping it by the worktree instance made the
    # seeded clone (keyed under the workspace `workspace`) invisible to the worktree
    # watcher, forcing a full re-embed. Track the WORKSPACE identity instead so the clone
    # is reused; the worktree instance_id still namespaces every container/network/runtime
    # path below. workspace_name mirrors the proxy the worktree instance_id itself uses.
    workspace_instance_id = provider_instance_id(
        "workspace",
        args.coordination_root,
        workspace_name=args.coordination_root.parent.name,
    )
    return {
        "enabled": True,
        "instance": {
            "id": instance_id,
            "scope": "worktree",
            "labels": provider_ownership_labels(
                provider_id=GREPAI_PROVIDER_ID,
                instance_id=instance_id,
                scope="worktree",
                coordination_root=args.coordination_root,
            ),
        },
        "workspace": scoped_name("agents-remember-memory", workspace_instance_id),
        "runtimeRoot": runtime_root.as_posix(),
        "requirementsFile": (
            args.coordination_root / "providers" / "requirements" / "grepai.txt"
        ).as_posix(),
        "stateFile": (runtime_root / "state" / "provider-state.json").as_posix(),
        "watch": {
            "mode": "background",
            "cwd": (isolated_root / "memory-roots").as_posix(),
            "logDir": log_root.as_posix(),
        },
        "allowMissingRoots": bool(getattr(args, "grepai_allow_missing_roots", False)),
    }


def _isolated_grepai_roots(
    provider: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    project_id: str,
    target_memory_root: Path,
) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    roots = provider.get("roots")
    if not isinstance(roots, list):
        roots = []
    replaced = False
    isolated_roots: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    for root in roots:
        normalized = _normalized_root(root)
        if normalized is None:
            continue
        if normalized["projectId"] == project_id:
            normalized["path"] = target_memory_root.as_posix()
            replaced = True
        isolated_roots.append(normalized)
    if not replaced:
        isolated_roots.append({"projectId": project_id, "path": target_memory_root.as_posix()})
    return isolated_roots


def _normalized_root(root: Any) -> dict[str, str] | None:
    if isinstance(root, str):
        return {"projectId": stable_provider_id(Path(root).name), "path": root}
    if not isinstance(root, dict):
        return None
    raw_path = str(root.get("path", ""))
    if not raw_path:
        return None
    project_id = stable_provider_id(
        str(root.get("projectId") or root.get("repoId") or Path(raw_path).name)
    )
    return {"projectId": project_id, "path": raw_path}


def _isolated_grepai_runtime(runtime_settings: Any, instance_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    version = GREPAI_PIN.split("==", 1)[1]
    runtime = runtime_settings if isinstance(runtime_settings, dict) else {}
    runtime = dict(runtime)
    runner = runtime.get("runner")
    runner = dict(runner) if isinstance(runner, dict) else {}
    runner.update(
        {
            "image": f"{GREPAI_RUNNER_IMAGE_REPOSITORY}:{version}",
            "containerName": scoped_name("ar-grepai-watcher", instance_id),
            "imageLockFile": "<coordination_root>/providers/requirements/grepai-runner-docker.lock",
            "buildRoot": "<runtimeRoot>/image",
            "runtimeMount": "/grepai/runtime",
            "logsMount": "/grepai/logs",
        }
    )
    runtime["mode"] = "docker"
    runtime["composeProject"] = scoped_name("agents-remember-grepai", instance_id)
    runtime["network"] = {"name": scoped_name(GREPAI_NETWORK_NAME, instance_id)}
    runtime["runner"] = runner
    return runtime


def _isolated_grepai_backend(
    args: Any,
    backend_settings: Any,
    *,
    isolated_root: Path,
    instance_id: str,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    backend = backend_settings if isinstance(backend_settings, dict) else {}
    backend = dict(backend)
    backend.update(
        {
            "runtimeRoot": (
                isolated_root / "providers" / "data" / "grepai" / instance_id / "postgres"
            ).as_posix(),
            "dataRoot": "<backendRuntimeRoot>/data",
            "image": "pgvector/pgvector:pg16",
            "imageLockFile": (
                args.coordination_root
                / "providers"
                / "requirements"
                / "grepai-postgres-docker.lock"
            ).as_posix(),
            "containerName": scoped_name("ar-grepai-postgres", instance_id),
            "postgres": {
                "user": "grepai",
                "password": "grepai",
                "database": "grepai",
            },
            "ports": {
                "postgres": {
                    "bindHost": "127.0.0.1",
                    "hostPort": "auto",
                    "containerPort": 5432,
                }
            },
        }
    )
    return backend


def _isolated_grepai_embedder(
    args: Any,
    embedder_settings: Any,
    *,
    isolated_root: Path,
    instance_id: str,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    embedder = embedder_settings if isinstance(embedder_settings, dict) else {}
    embedder = dict(embedder)
    ollama_container = scoped_name("ar-grepai-ollama", instance_id)
    # The worktree ollama starts with an empty model store. Rather than re-pulling the
    # ~274MB embedding model over the network for every worktree, seed it locally from the
    # already-running workspace ollama (the model is immutable shared content; the worktree's
    # vectors stay isolated in its own postgres). The watcher only pulls as a fallback.
    workspace_instance_id = provider_instance_id(
        "workspace",
        args.coordination_root,

# Shared STE-inspired writing profile

## Purpose and selected principles

Curators and explainer authors use this single profile for invariant statements, family guarantees,
history reasons and walkthrough prose. It selects clarity principles from
[ASD-STE100](https://asd-ste100.org/about_STE.html); it does not claim full ASD-STE100 compliance,
an "80 percent" measurement or a new controlled-language standard.

Name the actor and use concrete verbs: say who must do what, not merely that something is handled.
Write one independently testable promise per invariant. A paragraph develops one idea. Sentences
normally target about 20–25 words; precision takes priority over sentence length. Keep an exact
technical identifier or essential qualification even when the sentence is longer. Never split an
invariant automatically to meet a word target: a split is an explicit authored semantic change.

State conditions and exceptions explicitly. Keep quantifiers and negation: "every", "only", "no"
and "must not" are part of the obligation, not words to trim. Repeat the same term for the same
concept. Prefer a short explanation to an invented synonym.

## Use the project's vocabulary

Read applicable existing term records and use the product's vocabulary; do not create a second
terminology registry. These explanations orient the author without replacing those records:

| Term | Use |
| --- | --- |
| invariant | One independently testable obligation, with its applicability, conditions and exclusions. |
| family | An authored record whose members support its own joint guarantee; not a directory grouping. |
| joint guarantee | What the members together promise that none promises alone. Do not concatenate their statements. |
| realization | An attributed code place that carries an obligation, with its own rationale and role. |
| proof | Recorded evidence of a particular tested facet; not a claim that every case is established. |
| history row | The existing writer's content-bound judgment about a subject and its change. |
| revision | The exact record version the judgment or comparison addresses; never a prose edit counter supplied by the author. |
| candidate | The exact proposed code and memory state under examination, not an assumed installed or landed state. |

Keep identifiers, quoted source text and admitted effect labels exact. Distinguish
missing, unexamined, unavailable and measured absence: respectively not supplied, not checked,
not readable/obtainable, and checked with no instance found in a stated scope. None establishes
another, and none proves equivalence.

## Separate the promise from its support

State the promise in `statement`. Keep applicability, essential conditions and exclusions in their
existing semantic fields. When the statement relies on those fields, make that connection clear;
read the statement and scope together. Do not remove a condition just because another display shows it.

Keep realizations, proofs, identities and authoring provenance in their existing structural owners.
A history reason explains the concrete change and its consequence; a task ID or "wording improved"
alone explains neither. Use the existing [handoff contract](../templates/curator-handoff-list.md):
producer-owned fields remain verbatim, including the original statement and evidence. Author a
proposed record rewrite separately; do not silently replace the statement the producer handed over.
The writer continues to own IDs, anchors, revisions and row mechanics.

## Independent meaning review before publication

Use the existing [independent fact-check](../criteria/onboarding-memory.md#om-2--independent-fact-check-of-curated-knowledge-second-reader-requirement-bound-mik-r53-rule-5),
not a style-specific gate. A clearer rewrite is never proof of preserved meaning.

1. Preserve the exact old revision, before text, semantic scope, source anchors and evidence identities.
   Bind the proposed text to that baseline and the exact candidate being examined.
2. Compare old and new actor, trigger, required behavior, forbidden behavior, quantifiers, conditions and exclusions.
   Name each facet explicitly, including an unchanged field that the new statement depends on.
3. A reader who wrote none of the drafts explains each promise without oral repair and checks
   concrete conforming, violating and boundary cases against both versions. The reader records
   each ambiguity, changed obligation, missing evidence and unresolved case, not just a verdict.
4. Propose `clarify` only after independent review establishes that the obligation stays the same.
   A real change uses the existing appropriate effect and writer/history/revision route. Do not
   classify an edit from its apparent size or its word count. A family change retains its own
   authored effect, guarantee, examined members and writer-owned revision.
5. Correct or explicitly classify every disputed case before the normal writer publishes.
   An ambiguous draft stays unaccepted and names the actor, quantifier, condition or case in dispute.
   An unreadable revision or missing evidence is a reported gap, never an equivalence judgment.

### Worked comparison and deliberate failures (illustrations, not pilot evidence)

Before: "For every landing, the landing owner must publish only the accepted code and memory trees;
if either tree differs from the accepted candidate, publication must be refused."

Proposed: "For every landing, the landing owner must publish only the accepted code and memory trees.
The owner must refuse publication if either tree differs from the accepted candidate."

The proposed draft names the same actor, every landing, the same allowed trees and the same refusal
trigger. Its author has not accepted equivalence. The independent reader must test at least these cases:

| Case | Required reading of both versions |
| --- | --- |
| Conforming | Both trees equal the accepted candidate: the owner may publish under the existing admission rules. This promise alone does not grant admission. |
| Violating | The owner publishes a different memory tree even though the code tree matches: the owner violates the refusal. |
| Boundary | Only one tree differs: "either" still requires refusal. No exception for a code-only match exists. |

| Draft fault | What the independent comparison must catch |
| --- | --- |
| Removed negation | Changing "must not publish a different tree" to "must publish a different tree" reverses forbidden behavior. |
| Changed quantifier | Replacing "every landing" with "normally at landing" permits previously forbidden exceptions. It is not a clarification. |
| Lost condition | Dropping "if either tree differs" changes the refusal trigger; removing it from scope or omitting its connection in the prose does not preserve it. |
| Unrecorded effect | Calling a changed obligation cosmetic, or publishing it without the appropriate authored effect and history route, leaves the change unaccepted. |
| Altered frozen row | Editing an old closed row to make the draft appear historical changes evidence, not meaning preservation. Retain the original bytes and use the normal new revision route. |

## Three-real-invariant pilot and adoption

Select three existing invariant revisions: a direct promise, a conditional or exception-bearing
promise, and an obligation used in an authored family guarantee. Preserve the exact before text,
revision, scope, source/evidence identities and family membership where relevant. Produce proposed
rewrites and the facet/case comparison above. Record source availability separately from semantic
review: a stored evidence pointer is not evidence that the pointed-to report was read or rerun.

Prototype on real records in shared scratch clones, never the official checkout. Keep a frozen
baseline and separate drafts. An independent reader must judge all three; the author's own table
is a proposal, not acceptance. Correct or classify every ambiguity before the normal admitted
writer publishes. Do not run the writer merely to demonstrate style, rewrite frozen history,
backfill closed rows, or bulk-rewrite existing records. Scratch-clone preparation and later writer
execution require their normal authorization and isolation; this guide grants neither.

After adoption, new or revised invariant statements, family guarantees, history reasons and
walkthrough prose use this profile. Migration authors link it from their procedure before waves
start; preserve every other leaf's required guidance rather than adding a second writing guide.
Existing frozen records and closed history remain inspectable at their original identities.
Guide edits follow normal source/copy checks and curation. The normal skill-copy generator carries
this reference; its composition entry is reference metadata, not another meaning authority.

There is no automatic semantic validator here. Word-count and vocabulary heuristics cannot approve,
reject or classify meaning. Schema, identity, admission, invariant gates and normal writer refusal
and retry behavior remain unchanged. This profile provides author/reviewer guidance and examples,
not a language gate or a closeout bypass.
# Curator — writer and authoring step detail

Read the serving-build command section before a CLI deciding run or write. Read the remaining
authoring detail when you reach **Curation workflow 2: Before ingest**, not before.
Its family/external-reference formats and read-back call are used at **Curation workflow 3: Group only justified obligations**.
The operation owns serving-build authority; this file supplies the command and its report semantics.

## Step 2 — serving-build command and options

Prefer the mounted `knowledge_write`. For a CLI deciding run or write, bind the command to the
starting server's `server_info.servingBuild` as `operations/curation.md` requires. Obtain the
original interpreter from the role launch receipt's `toolServer.command[0]`, or the selected
server's startup definition's `command`. Preserve that spelling: `servingBuild.pythonExecutable`

dependencies. If the admitted launch command is unavailable, report the CLI binding unavailable;
do not infer it from the resolved path or install another build.

Fill these values from that launch and the starting `server_info`, then print the CLI's identity:

```sh

AR_SERVING_PACKAGE='<server_info.servingBuild.packageRoot>'

Keep an unreported commit unknown, never call it a verified clean checkout.

Use the same interpreter and explicit package path for the public CLI commands:

```sh
PYTHONPATH="$AR_SERVING_PARENT" "$AR_SERVING_PYTHON" -P -m agents_remember.cli \
  knowledge-worklist --contract '<this leaf enclosure contract>'
PYTHONPATH="$AR_SERVING_PARENT" "$AR_SERVING_PYTHON" -P -m agents_remember.cli \

## Step 2 — check messages

## Step 2 — weakness and dependent records

**A weakness and a dependent are recorded through the writer, as every record.** An entry of kind `weakness` in a producer's hand-off list becomes a `WKN-` record through the writer, or the report says why not: the writer refuses one without a file, with an unknown kind, or with a statement beyond its one-sentence bound, and the refusal names the field. """CodeGraphContext provider setup facade."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from agents_remember.kernel.primitives.identity import (
    provider_instance_id,
    provider_ownership_labels,
    scoped_name,
)
from agents_remember.providers.cgc.seed import (
    CGC_PROVIDER_ID,
    cgc_extra_args,
    cgc_seed_bundle,
)
from agents_remember.providers.context import (
    CGC_NETWORK_NAME,
    CGC_WATCHER_CONTAINER_PREFIX,
)
from agents_remember.providers.setup_common import (
    LifecycleCommand,
    provider_settings,
    run_lifecycle,
    selected_provider_enabled,
    setup_progress_from,
    stable_provider_id,
)
from agents_remember.providers.setup_progress import SetupProgress


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class IsolatedCgcOptions:
    runtime_root: Path | None = None
    settings_path: Path | None = None
    container_name: str | None = None


def isolated_cgc_settings(
    args: Any,
    settings: dict[str, Any],
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    if args.cgc_isolated_runtime_root is None:
        return None

    provider = provider_settings(settings, CGC_PROVIDER_ID)
    if provider is None:
        return None
    _require_isolated_target_root(args)
    cgc = _isolated_cgc_provider(args, provider)
    return _isolated_settings_payload(cgc)


def _require_isolated_target_root(args: Any) -> None:
    if args.cgc_seed_target_repo_root is None:
        raise RuntimeError("--cgc-isolated-runtime-root requires --cgc-seed-target-repo-root")


def _isolated_settings_payload(cgc: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "version": 1,
        "contextProviders": {
            "enabled": True,
            "providers": {
                CGC_PROVIDER_ID: cgc,
            },
            "policy": {
                "discoveryOnly": True,
                "sourceProofRequired": True,
            },
        },
    }


def _isolated_cgc_provider(args: Any, provider: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    isolated_root = args.cgc_isolated_runtime_root.resolve()
    repo_id = stable_provider_id(args.cgc_seed_repo_id or args.cgc_seed_target_repo_root.name)
    instance_id = provider_instance_id(
        "worktree",
        isolated_root,
        workspace_name=args.coordination_root.parent.name,
    )
    cgc = json.loads(json.dumps(provider))
    cgc.update(_isolated_cgc_base_fields(args, isolated_root, repo_id, instance_id))
    cgc["runtime"] = _isolated_cgc_runtime(cgc.get("runtime"), instance_id)
    cgc["backend"] = _isolated_cgc_backend(
        args,
        cgc.get("backend"),
        isolated_root,
        repo_id,
        instance_id,
    )
    return cgc


def _isolated_cgc_base_fields(
    args: Any,
    isolated_root: Path,
    repo_id: str,
    instance_id: str,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    runtime_root = isolated_root / "providers" / "runners" / "codegraphcontext" / instance_id
    log_file = (
        isolated_root
        / "logs"
        / "providers"
        / "codegraphcontext"
        / instance_id
        / "<repoId>"
        / "watch.log"
    )
    return {
        "enabled": True,
        "instance": {
            "id": instance_id,
            "scope": "worktree",
            "labels": provider_ownership_labels(
                provider_id=CGC_PROVIDER_ID,
                instance_id=instance_id,
                scope="worktree",
                coordination_root=args.coordination_root,
            ),
        },
        "roots": [
            {
                "repoId": repo_id,
                "path": args.cgc_seed_target_repo_root.resolve().as_posix(),
            }
        ],
        "runtimeRoot": runtime_root.as_posix(),
        "instanceRootTemplate": "<runtimeRoot>/<repoId>",
        "requirementsFile": (
            args.coordination_root / "providers" / "requirements" / "codegraphcontext.txt"
        ).as_posix(),
        "patchesRoot": (
            args.coordination_root / "providers" / "patches" / "codegraphcontext"
        ).as_posix(),
        "stateFileTemplate": "<instanceRoot>/provider-state.json",
        "watch": {
            "mode": "managed-foreground",
            "cwdTemplate": "<instanceRoot>",
            "logFileTemplate": log_file.as_posix(),
        },
    }


def _isolated_cgc_runtime(runtime_settings: Any, instance_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    runtime = runtime_settings if isinstance(runtime_settings, dict) else {}
    runtime = dict(runtime)
    runner = runtime.get("runner")
    runner = dict(runner) if isinstance(runner, dict) else {}
    runner["buildRoot"] = "<runtimeRoot>/image"
    runner["containerNameTemplate"] = (
        f"{scoped_name(CGC_WATCHER_CONTAINER_PREFIX, instance_id)}-<repoId>"
    )
    runtime["mode"] = "docker"
    runtime["composeProject"] = scoped_name("agents-remember-cgc", instance_id)
    runtime["runner"] = runner
    return runtime


def _isolated_cgc_backend(
    args: Any,
    backend_settings: Any,
    isolated_root: Path,
    repo_id: str,
    instance_id: str,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    backend = backend_settings if isinstance(backend_settings, dict) else {}
    backend = dict(backend)
    backend.update(
        {
            "runtimeRoot": (
                isolated_root / "providers" / "data" / "codegraphcontext" / instance_id / "falkordb"
            ).as_posix(),
            "dataRoot": "<backendRuntimeRoot>/data",
            "imageLockFile": (
                isolated_root
                / "providers"
                / "requirements"
                / "codegraphcontext-falkordb-docker.lock"
            ).as_posix(),
            "containerName": _isolated_cgc_container_name(args, instance_id, repo_id),
            "network": {"name": scoped_name(CGC_NETWORK_NAME, instance_id)},
        }
    )
    return backend


def _isolated_cgc_container_name(args: Any, instance_id: str, repo_id: str) -> str:
    return args.cgc_isolated_container_name or scoped_name("ar-cgc-falkordb", instance_id, repo_id)


def write_isolated_cgc_settings(
    args: Any,
    settings: dict[str, Any],
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    data = isolated_cgc_settings(args, settings)
    if data is None:
        args.cgc_from_settings = None
        return None

    path = args.cgc_isolated_settings_path or (
        args.cgc_isolated_runtime_root.resolve()
        / "settings"
        / "codegraphcontext-provider-settings.json"
    )
    args.cgc_from_settings = path.resolve()
    if not args.dry_run:
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return {
        "path": args.cgc_from_settings.as_posix(),
        "dryRun": args.dry_run,
        "settings": data if args.dry_run else None,
    }


def install_enabled_provider(args: Any, settings: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    if not selected_provider_enabled(args, settings, CGC_PROVIDER_ID):
        return []
    progress = setup_progress_from(args)
    progress.phase_start("codegraphcontext", "install-all")
    result = run_lifecycle(
        args.coordination_root,
        LifecycleCommand(
            provider="cgc",
            action="install-all",
            extra_args=tuple(cgc_extra_args(args)),
        ),
        timeout=args.timeout,
        dry_run=args.dry_run,
    )
    progress.phase_done(result)
    return [result]


def prepare_enabled_provider(args: Any, settings: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    if not selected_provider_enabled(args, settings, CGC_PROVIDER_ID):
        return []
    progress = setup_progress_from(args)
    progress.phase_start("codegraphcontext", "seed", note="graph copy from workspace (seconds)")
    seed = cgc_seed_bundle(args, settings)
    seed_result = {"provider": "codegraphcontext", "action": "seed", **seed}
    progress.phase_done(seed_result)
    results = [seed_result]
    results.append(_refresh_after_seed(args, seed, progress))
    return results


def _seed_failure_reason(seed: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    reason = seed.get("reason")
    if reason:
        return str(reason)
    stage = seed.get("stage")
    return f"seed failed at {stage}" if stage else "seed failed"


def _refresh_after_seed(args: Any, seed: dict[str, Any], progress: SetupProgress) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if seed.get("ok"):
        return {
            "ok": True,
            "provider": "codegraphcontext",
            "action": "refresh-all",
            "skipped": True,
            "reason": "CGC seed loaded successfully",
        }
    if args.cgc_refresh_fallback:
        # The single most important transition to surface (GitHub #53): a refused
        # seed changes the expected duration from ~1 minute to N minutes, and the
        # reindex itself emits nothing the orchestrator can see.
        progress.phase_start(
            "codegraphcontext",
            "refresh-all",
            note="full reindex fallback; duration scales with repo size (minutes)",
            seed_fallback={"active": True, "reason": _seed_failure_reason(seed)},
        )
        result = run_lifecycle(
            args.coordination_root,
            LifecycleCommand(
                provider="cgc",
                action="refresh-all",
                extra_args=tuple(cgc_extra_args(args)),
            ),
            timeout=args.timeout,
            dry_run=args.dry_run,
        )
        progress.phase_done(result)
        return result
    return {
        "ok": False,
        "provider": "codegraphcontext",
        "action": "refresh-all",
        "skipped": True,
        "reason": "CGC seed failed and refresh fallback is disabled",
    }
